quotes.how: parsed with the same routine as scripts/overlay-verdict-claims.test.mjs#intentCriteria and by scripts/navigation-capture.test.mjs#intentCriteria, so every criterionText below is the intent's own text and not a paraphrase; the pin that holds it compares character for character

why: No row is required, and the list therefore names no driver, no instance and no verdict path: scripts/overlay-verdict-claims.test.mjs refuses a list with no required row that names a driver, so naming one would be the opposite defect.

The reason is not convenience. A required row must name the driver a control-ai-browsers run expression takes to the wave gate, and that driver must return the gate's four readings — toolElements, drawnRect, descriptor and noDevContext — with the required rows together citing drawnRect, descriptor and noDevContext, because that is the reading set the overlay driver produces. This milestone's readings are router events on the page's own stream and the finding a join writes from them. Naming spikes/probes/overlay-pick.js as their driver would make the gate return overlay measurements for navigation criteria, which is the re-cut N6 forbids; a navigation driver does not exist in this repository and this task may not add one.

The portal measurements are not lost: they are the recording the criteria are checked against, taken on the zoneless portal at http://localhost:4507/ (commands.serve, environment.portal, branch claude/ai-devtools-spike at 92d46ec) and on the counter fixture at http://localhost:4222/, and every row above names the artefact it is carried by and the command that proves it.

claims.criterionText: On the portal, a navigation the agent recorded and that reached a terminal event produces a finding naming the route it was heading for (`url`), the route it ended on when that event carried `urlAfterRedirects`, and the terminal event's own class — `NavigationEnd`, `NavigationCancel`, `NavigationError` or `NavigationSkipped` — carrying only the fields that event recorded (`code` and `reason`, or the error's own name and message), and naming no other cause.
claims.asserts: A navigation the agent recorded and that reached a terminal event is reported as the terminal event it reached — NavigationEnd, NavigationCancel, NavigationError or NavigationSkipped — naming the route it was heading for from the terminal event's own `url`, naming an end route only where that event carried `urlAfterRedirects`, carrying only that event's own fields (a cancel's or a skip's `code` and `reason`, an error's own `name` and `message`), and naming no cause beyond them.
claims.artefact: research/raw/m041-navigation.json (terminals.cancel, terminals.error, terminals.skip, terminals.redirect, warm.terminal) -> extension/navigation-narrator.js -> apps/angular-ai-devtools/src/app/panel-navigation.ts
claims.proves: node --experimental-strip-types --test "scripts/navigation-blocking.test.mjs" (E1, E2) and npx nx run angular-ai-devtools:test (panel-demo.spec.ts holds the rendered lines to the recording)
claims.reason: A portal route does produce the navigation this criterion is measured on — the recording's warm frame is /claim/list on the zoneless portal at http://localhost:4507/ (environment.portal, commands.serve) — but the criterion's fact is the finding the join writes from the agent's record, and no insurance-portal route renders a finding: the surface that renders it is served from apps/angular-ai-devtools and inspects the portal, so CHARTER.md's portal clause has no page-side fact of this criterion to reach. What carries the claim is research/raw/m041-navigation.json (terminals.cancel, terminals.error, terminals.skip and warm.terminal, each keeping the keys its own event carried and no others) joined by extension/navigation-narrator.js and rendered by apps/angular-ai-devtools/src/app/panel-navigation.ts. The command that proves it is node --experimental-strip-types --test "scripts/navigation-blocking.test.mjs", whose E1 and E2 pins render each of the four terminal classes as itself and refuse an end route a NavigationCancel did not carry, with npx nx run angular-ai-devtools:test holding the rendered lines to the recording. A portal-backed verdict for it would take the same page events this milestone already recorded and still not produce the finding, which is the artefact the criterion names.

claims.criterionText: A navigation that recorded a `NavigationStart` and no terminal event produces an open-navigation finding naming the stage of its last recorded event — route-config load, guards check, resolve or activation — as the stage reached, and never as the reason it is open.
claims.asserts: A navigation that recorded a NavigationStart and no terminal event is reported open, naming the stage of its last recorded event — route-config load, guards check, resolve or activation — as the stage reached and never as the reason it is open.
claims.artefact: research/raw/m041-navigation.json (held.inFlight: NavigationStart at 198.9 ms then RouteConfigLoadStart at 199.4 ms, no terminal, router.url still /home) -> extension/navigation-narrator.js -> apps/angular-ai-devtools/src/app/panel-navigation.ts
claims.reason: The portal is the page whose held navigation this criterion is written on — held.inFlight was measured on the zoneless portal with every .js request delayed 2,500 ms — but the criterion's fact is the open-navigation finding, which no portal route renders: the portal page is what is being narrated, and the finding is produced by extension/navigation-narrator.js from the agent's record and rendered by apps/angular-ai-devtools/src/app/panel-navigation.ts. CHARTER.md's portal clause therefore has no route whose facts this criterion names; a verdict driven against the portal would return the events the recording already carries and not the finding the criterion asserts. What carries the claim is research/raw/m041-navigation.json held.inFlight together with the narrator's stage table. The command that proves it is node --experimental-strip-types --test "scripts/navigation-blocking.test.mjs", whose E3 pin renders a start with no terminal open at its last stage and an empty record as the absence rather than as zero kinds, and whose E4 pin requires every rendered stage word to be the name of an event the record contains; node --experimental-strip-types --test "scripts/panel-navigation.test.mjs" holds the pane to one block per navigation.

claims.criterionText: The holder of an open navigation is reported as cannot-tell with the named absence `no-holder-recorded`, because no router event payload and no field of `currentNavigation()` names a guard, a resolver, a chunk or a task; no finding names what is holding an in-flight navigation.
claims.asserts: The holder of an open navigation is cannot-tell with the named absence `no-holder-recorded`, because no router event payload and no field of currentNavigation() names a guard, a resolver, a chunk or a task, and no finding names what is holding an in-flight navigation.
claims.artefact: research/raw/m041-navigation.json (absences["no-holder-recorded"]: the 10 currentNavigation() fields at the hold, the 2 the chunk adds later, payloadFieldsMatchingAWord empty) -> extension/navigation-narrator.js (no-holder-recorded) -> apps/angular-ai-devtools/src/app/panel-navigation.ts
claims.reason: This criterion is a claim about what the portal does not carry: measured on the zoneless portal during the 2,500 ms hold, currentNavigation() returned ten fields — abort, beforeActivateHandler, extractedUrl, extras, id, initialUrl, previousNavigation, routesRecognizeHandler, targetBrowserUrl, trigger — and the two events recorded during the hold carried six payload keys between them, none of which matches guard, resolver, chunk, task or holder. The portal route produces the absence, and the absence is recorded; what no portal route renders is the cannot-tell finding that names it, which is the join's answer (extension/navigation-narrator.js) rendered by apps/angular-ai-devtools/src/app/panel-navigation.ts. CHARTER.md's portal clause therefore does not reach the criterion's own fact. The command that proves it is node --experimental-strip-types --test "scripts/navigation-blocking.test.mjs", whose E5 pin requires an open navigation's holder to be no-holder-recorded and forbids a guard, chunk or task name beside it, and node --experimental-strip-types --test "scripts/panel-navigation.test.mjs", which holds the same separation at the pane.

claims.criterionText: A guard's verdict is cannot-tell with the named absence `guard-verdict-not-recorded` — the only guard field the stream carries is the aggregate `GuardsCheckEnd.shouldActivate`, a guard refusal reaches the same wildcard `RoutesRecognized` and `NavigationEnd` as an unmatched URL, and a guard is named only when the configured function carries a name — and a resolver stage on a configuration that declares no resolver is cannot-tell with `no-resolver-configured`.
claims.asserts: A guard's verdict is cannot-tell with the named absence `guard-verdict-not-recorded` — the only guard field the stream carries is the aggregate GuardsCheckEnd.shouldActivate, a guard refusal reaches the same wildcard RoutesRecognized and NavigationEnd as an unmatched URL, and a guard is named only when the configured function carries a name — and a resolver stage on a configuration that declares no resolver is cannot-tell with `no-resolver-configured`.
claims.artefact: research/raw/m041-navigation.json (absences["guard-verdict-not-recorded"] with its 11-event refused-versus-unmatched comparison, absences["no-resolver-configured"] with 0 resolve keys across 23 portal rows and 20 fixture rows, guards.fixture.canActivateNames ["redirectGuard"]) -> extension/navigation-narrator.js -> apps/angular-ai-devtools/src/app/panel-navigation.ts
claims.reason: Both named absences were measured on the portal: the portal's own manifest served with claim-list false produced the same eleven events, the same key sets, the same wildcard chain [null,"**"], the same shouldActivate true and the same NavigationEnd as an unmatched URL, with no NavigationCancel in either, and the portal declares 0 resolve keys across 23 walked rows while still emitting ResolveStart and ResolveEnd. The portal produces those facts; what it does not render is the cannot-tell finding that names them, which is extension/navigation-narrator.js's answer rendered by apps/angular-ai-devtools/src/app/panel-navigation.ts, so CHARTER.md's portal clause does not reach the criterion's own fact. The command that proves it is node --experimental-strip-types --test "scripts/navigation-blocking.test.mjs", whose E6 pin reports the wildcard match and never "a guard refused" and gives an anonymous canMatch no name, and whose E7 pin renders shouldActivate as the aggregate it is and the resolve stage with no-resolver-configured; node --experimental-strip-types --test "scripts/panel-navigation.test.mjs" holds the same two absences at the pane.

claims.criterionText: A navigation that completed is never reported as held: a long `RouteConfigLoadStart → RouteConfigLoadEnd` gap is reported with the interval those two events measured and the terminal event that followed, and a `RouteConfigLoadStart` with no matching end is reported open at the route-config-load stage without borrowing a navigation id, because those two events carry `route` and `type` and no `id`.
claims.asserts: A completed navigation is never reported as held: a long RouteConfigLoadStart to RouteConfigLoadEnd gap is reported with the interval those two events measured and the terminal event that followed, and a RouteConfigLoadStart with no matching end is reported open at the route-config-load stage without borrowing a navigation id, because those two events carry `route` and `type` and no `id`.
claims.artefact: research/raw/m041-navigation.json (warm.routeConfigLoads: claim 15.6 ms and list 37.6 ms with NavigationEnd at 424.9 ms; superseded.ordering: the abandoned load end 1192.1 ms after its own cancel and 314.8 ms before the successor's; held.completion) -> extension/navigation-narrator.js -> apps/angular-ai-devtools/src/app/panel-navigation.ts
claims.reason: The intervals this criterion reports were measured on the portal — /claim/list opened with a 15.6 ms and a 37.6 ms route-config interval and ended NavigationEnd, and the superseded run put the abandoned navigation's own load end 1192.1 ms after its cancel and 314.8 ms before the successor's — and both facts are in the recording. What no portal route renders is the report: the joined answer that prints an interval beside the terminal event that followed it, or an open load at the route-config-load stage with no borrowed id, is extension/navigation-narrator.js's and apps/angular-ai-devtools/src/app/panel-navigation.ts's, so CHARTER.md's portal clause does not reach the criterion's own fact. The command that proves it is node --experimental-strip-types --test "scripts/navigation-blocking.test.mjs", whose E8 pin renders a completed navigation with its measured interval as ended and never open, and whose E9 pin refuses an id to a RouteConfigLoadStart and refuses to attribute a superseded navigation's late load end to its successor; node --experimental-strip-types --test "scripts/panel-navigation.test.mjs" holds each route-config load to its own route and its own interval.

claims.asserts: The project gate passes at the head of the milestone: `npm run check` and `npm test` both exit zero at the landed commit, with the claim list and the recording present.

What carries the claim is research/raw/m041-verdict-claims.json, this file, which is what lets scripts/overlay-verdict-claims.test.mjs check the milestone's claims instead of failing on a missing recording, together with research/raw/m041-navigation.json and the suites the milestone landed. The command that proves it is npm run check && npm test, and its result is recorded in T005's Log and in .project/build/verify-ledger.jsonl rather than claimed here.
